L-glessner-court-ground-2224
      Courtyard approaches and cut lawn edges
      
    
    
    Decision
    Reconstruct functional July 1904 circulation from the cleared HABS sheet 2 gate, passage and stair positions. That plan does not survey garden paths. The straight drive now joins the two recorded openings directly, replacing the previous photograph-based intermediate bend. Rights-uncleared HABS05 supplies no new derived path geometry. The HABS written account, printed page 2, dates complete parking paving to September 1946; it is excluded from the 1904 scene. The pedestrian approaches are our bounded reconstruction: a four-foot walk along the west service wing turns toward the north stair, and a separate narrow approach joins the existing curved terrace foot. The west route accommodates the court-side stair whose chronology and final geometry remain T-2228; it does not copy the separate wooden stair behind the stable, explicitly added about 1955. These paths are functional choices, not a photographed 1904 garden design. Pale compacted gravel is separately reconstructed as a plausible permeable surface; the plan identifies neither gravel nor a paving specification. The existing procedural gravel and turf textures are retained, without photographic pixels or later parking slabs. The gate and passage retain the approximately 36.6 mm drive top. The west wall side of its path rises by 7.3 mm across 1.2192 m, falling toward the lawn with a short entry transition. There is no invented buried drain network or drain-cover pattern. Cut lawn margins meet the closed gravel edge; the lawn remains approximately 15.2 mm above the local datum. Solid stair, pier, bay, bow, terrace and tower footprints and all hard surfaces are excluded from turf. Inscribed ground cuts may continue up to about 63 mm beneath solid curved masonry, simplifying invisible geometry; grass clearance uses the physical curves and rough tower footing extent. Computational mesh seams are not grass borders. Full and Light share circulation and contacts; Full retains its bounded 20,000 grass-blade budget. Every new face is reconstructed. The owner's granite tint and dark glass are unchanged. This supersedes L295's ground layout basis for the current v4 model, without rewriting that historical decision.
    Ticket
    T-2224.
